about: How Troupe.Protocol.PermissionRule reads each rule and each set, sentence for sentence. permission_rule_test.exs holds the module to it and the console's rules editor (clients/gui/packages/client/src/rules.ts) is held to it by rules.test.ts, so the editor checks a rule as the plane will.

rules.refused: a rule names a tool, such as shell or shell(git push)
a rule names a tool, such as shell or shell(git push)
"shell(git push" opens a bracket it does not close; a rule is a tool or tool(pattern)
"shell git" is not a rule; a rule is a tool, or a tool with a pattern in brackets: shell(git push)
Bash is another tool's name for it; Troupe's is shell, as in shell(...)
WebFetch is another tool's name for it; Troupe's is web_fetch, as in web_fetch(...)
MultiEdit is another tool's name for it; Troupe's is edit_file, as in edit_file(...)
a tool's name is lower case: grep, not Grep
"my-tool" is not a tool's name; a name is lower-case letters, digits and _
an MCP server's tool is written mcp(github.create_issue), not mcp.github.create_issue
an MCP server's tool is written mcp(notes.search), not client.notes.search, whoever hosts it
shell() has an empty pattern, which matches nothing; write shell for every call, or a pattern in the brackets
shell() has an empty pattern, which matches nothing; write shell for every call, or a pattern in the brackets
shell(git * --force): a shell rule is a command prefix, which * may only end, as in git push*
shell(npm test:*): drop the :*, since shell(npm test) already matches every command that starts with it
web_fetch takes no pattern; only shell (a command prefix), the file tools (read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_files, grep, glob, git_read: a path) and mcp (server.tool) do. Write web_fetch alone
mcp(git hub): an MCP rule names server.tool, or a server alone, such as mcp(github.create_*)

refused: permissions.ask is a list of rules, such as ["shell(git push)"]
permissions.deny: Bash is another tool's name for it; Troupe's is shell, as in shell(...)
permissions.deny: shell() has an empty pattern, which matches nothing; write shell for every call, or a pattern in the brackets
permissions takes allow, ask and deny, not nope
